I will do it the way I have been doing on this land, with small changes if I think it can hold yield. I have 10.9 mu, not tiny and not very big, so I cannot throw money around, but I also cannot be stingy and lose grain. On wheat, I will still use the improved seed most people around me use, because if neighbors plant it and fill the ears well, I trust that more than talk. I will put the main fertilizer before or at sowing, then give urea again at the turning-green stage. Wheat drinks water at key times, so with well water in hand I will not save on those few irrigations. If the field gets rust, aphids, or later dry hot wind stress, the loss is bigger than one more input bill. After wheat harvest, maize goes in right away. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because around here that is normal now and the ears are fuller. I will keep fertilizer a little on the safe side, because if maize goes hungry in a dry hot stretch, yield drops fast and I cannot get it back. I will watch what nearby farmers do, and if they all spray once more for armyworm or leaf disease, I will do the same. On this kind of wheat-maize land, I will keep the work simple: wheat with rotary tillage, maize mostly no-tillage after wheat harvest so I do not miss moisture or sowing time.
